chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Ali ibn Abdullah al-Hannat, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from al-Kalbi al-Nassab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Permissible.' I said, 'We soak it, so we throw into it the residue (of an intoxicant) and what is besides that.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shh! Shh! That is the rotten wine.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so which al-Nabeez do you mean?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The people of Al-Medina complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of the changed water and spoiling of their health. So he (peace be upon him) ordered them that they should be drinking al-Nabeez. So the man from them was instructing his servant that he should make al-Nabeez for him, so he would extend his handful of dates, so he would cast these in the container. So from it, he would be drinking, and from it he would be purifying.'

So I said, 'And how much was the number of the dates which was cast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever a palm could gather.' I said, 'One and two?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes it was one, and sometimes it was two.' So I said, 'And how much was the capacity of the container of water?' (He (peace be upon him) said): 'What is between forty to eighty, to what is above that?' So I said, 'By the Ratls (A unit of measurement)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ratls by the measurement of Al-Iraq.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-Nabeez and how is it distinguished from wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the distinction between permissible al-Nabeez and intoxicating wine by addressing the specific practice of the people of Medina, who soaked a handful of dates in water to mitigate bodily impurities. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the base preparation was allowed, the accumulation of residue and fermentation led to its classification as 'rotten wine' when consumed in excess, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the quantity and quality of ingredients in determining legal status. The detailed discussion on measurements (a handful of dates and 40-80 Iraqi artals of water) provides a practical framework for understanding the transition from non-intoxicating to intoxicating states.
